narrative.overview:
Second Look is the same sky checked night after night and written down. The world is built from an almanac's own materials: navy book cloth for the ground, page-white ink for everything read, and a single rubric red that marks the second look. Everything is flat colour on a flat ground; discs and tabular figures carry the content, and nothing glows.

The signature is two looks. In the logo, two page-white rings overlap, and only the lens they share is red; on the banner, the red element is the full Moon that closes the row of phases. Red always marks what the second look reveals, and it is the only red. The mark is symmetric on both axes. The system deliberately refuses the space-channel default of nebula photography, neon type and glowing planets.

Density is low and calm. Each artifact says one thing in large type, with generous navy around it, and lets one precise figure row do the work of decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Three achromatic-feeling materials (cloth, page, ink-soft) plus one reserved accent (rubric).
One variable family, Archivo, used at two widths: expanded and black for the wordmark, normal width for everything else.
Flat fills only: no gradients, no shadows, no glow, no strokes.
One red reveal per artifact (the lens where the logo's rings overlap; the full Moon ending the phase row) is the one recurring device.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Each artifact carries exactly one rubric-red element: what the second look reveals (the logo's lens, the banner's full Moon). Red is never a highlight, a button, an underline, a word, or decoration.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: Secondary tones are mixed from the cloth's own blue. Never introduce a neutral grey.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number is set with tabular figures (tnum), whether in HTML text or SVG labels.

rules.name: The Two Widths Rule
rules.body: Expanded width belongs to the wordmark alone. All other text stays at 100% width.

rules.name: The Flat Print Rule
rules.body: If it could not be printed with flat inks on book cloth, it does not belong here.

dos: Do use cloth as the full-bleed ground of every artifact.
Do use exactly one rubric element per artifact: the reveal (the logo's lens, the banner's full Moon).
Do use Archivo for all text, expanded and black only for the wordmark.
Do set every number in tabular figures, and compute figures from real data rather than typing decorative numbers.
Do separate tones by fill (cloth vs cloth-lift) instead of outlines.
Do keep everything that must be read inside the platform's safe area.
donts: Don't use red for text, highlights, underlines, icons or a second accent.
Don't add gradients, glow, blur, shadows or strokes.
Don't use nebula or starfield photography, neon type, or glowing planets.
Don't introduce neutral greys or a second display face.
